er_v06_c11_b001_01: She drags the sack up below the window, leaving a dusty streak on the ground.
er_v06_c11_b001_02: I've been to the one at the docks. The scale's crooked.
er_v06_c11_b001_03: He weighs wire by the pound, then pulls two strands off the top and calls it loss.
er_v06_c11_b001_04: I put it back in the bag right there and walked out.
er_v06_c11_b001_05: She turns the sack upside down and shakes it out. Shells and connectors scatter on the counter, lined up in three rows by condition.
er_v06_c11_b001_06: Left side works as is. Middle needs repair. Right side is shells only.
er_v06_c11_b001_07: You quote a price. If it's wrong, I'll say so.
er_v06_c11_b001_08: Two in the middle row are good.
er_v06_c11_b001_10: The shopkeeper slides two connectors into the left row. She bends close, nose almost touching the counter.
er_v06_c11_b001_11: ...The rust's on the outer ring. The inside's bright.
er_v06_c11_b001_13: The coins slide across. She unties the change pouch at her waist and pours the coins from the counter and the pouch together.
er_v06_c11_b001_15: Seven hundred sixty... seven hundred eighty...
er_v06_c11_b001_16: She flips the pouch over and pats it twice. The last few coins drop out, gray with scrapyard dust.
er_v06_c11_b001_19: Still around my neck. I took it out to look when I was two coins short.
er_v06_c11_b001_21: The shopkeeper pulls a clean cloth from under the counter and sets it by her hand.
er_v06_c11_b001_22: For wiping my hands? The dirt on my hands is none of your concern.
er_v06_c11_b001_23: She picks up the cloth anyway and wipes each finger, one by one, even between them.
er_v06_c11_b001_24: The detective sees me tomorrow. I'll bring the money myself.
er_v06_c11_b001_25: Don't follow me. If he sees someone with me, his price changes.
